rendered:
Among the reviews, only the cobalt-free cathode review (aenm-2022) cites its own references on disordered rock-salt (DRX) cathodes. That count is 11[1] references, in an unbroken run in its reference list. The run starts with [34] R. J. Clément, Z. Lun, G. Ceder, Energy Environ. Sci. 2020, 13, 345.[2] and ends with [44] A. Abdellahi, A. Urban, S. Dacek, G. Ceder, Chem. Mater. 2016, 28, 5373.[3] Its section 5. DRX Cathodes[4] and the captions of Fig. 8[5] and Fig. 9[6] cite these references.

I didn't count these other citations:
- The same section also cites [27] A. Manthiram, Nat. Commun. 2020, 11, 1550.[7] This is a general cathode reference, used for the common view that a high degree of Li/TM ordering is needed.[8]
- The review's introduction cites a group of references for layered, spinel, olivine and DRX systems together, not for DRX alone.[9]

The other reviews have no DRX references:
- The surface-coating review (ensm-2021) mentions disordered rock salt type[10] cathodes only once, in its conclusions, and cites nothing for them.
- My search of the roll-to-roll manufacturing perspective (ensm-2020) found no mention of DRX or disordered rock-salt cathodes.
